item: A ratchet sends a foreign Origin to every state-changing operation of the OpenAPI schema and asserts the middleware's 403 (audit 0.5.0 item 35 follow-on)
refs: coordinator 27 Oct 00:11: start the origin-guard ratchet, new file, floor = today's count; R252 proposal item 35
summary: tests/test_origin_guard_every_route.py walks the app's own OpenAPI schema (317 POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE operations on 2026-10-27, floor 317) and asserts that a request carrying Origin http://evil.example answers the Origin middleware's own 403 body before any handler runs; a foreign Referer alone is refused on one operation per method; the /static and /metrics mounts are driven by hand for all four methods; and the same request with this server's own Origin, or with neither header, reaches the handler (400 on remove-imported) so the loop cannot pass on a blanket 403. On the routes with no body or an optional one (159 of 317) and the six raw-body modules this check is the only layer that stands (docs/SECURITY.md). RED-WITHOUT shown: exempting /api/jobs from the middleware makes the test fail naming the four /api/jobs operations (404/422 reached the handler). Passes today on all 317: no finding. Limits: operations with include_in_schema=False are not listed (the three that exist are GETs); only the Origin and Referer headers are driven, not the middleware's scheme/port logic (tests/test_security_hardening.py).
